raw_response:
Aiya, you want to know how I'll farm this year? Let me think it through. I've been doing this 55 years, so mostly I just do what worked before.

**My land.** I have 5 mu altogether. About 3 mu I do wheat in winter and maize in summer — same as everyone in the village. The other 2 mu I keep for cotton, on the sandier piece near the road. Cotton is more trouble but the price has been okay some years, and it spreads my risk — if the wheat is bad I still have something.

**Wheat (3 mu).** I planted last October already, around the 10th, like always. Used the seed I bought from the agro-shop, the same kind my neighbor Old Wang uses — he gets good wheat so I follow him. Before planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu (the 15-15-15 kind). When the wheat starts jointing in March, I'll topdress about half a bag of urea per mu — if it looks yellow I'll add a bit more, if it looks dark green I save the money. I water it maybe 3 times — once before winter, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. The well is right there but the electricity for pumping isn't free, so I don't water more than I need. Harvest beginning of June. I expect maybe 400 kg per mu, sometimes 450 if the spring rain is good.

**Maize (3 mu).** Right after wheat harvest, no time to rest. I hire the neighbor with the small combine to harvest the wheat and then I get my son back from town for two days to help me plant maize directly into the stubble. Hybrid seed, the Zhengdan kind, what the seed shop pushes. I put one bag of compound at planting and then about half a bag of urea per mu when it's knee-high. Usually no irrigation if the summer rains come — only if July is dry I'll water once. Harvest end of September. Last year I got maybe 450 kg per mu, that's normal.

**Cotton (2 mu).** This is the hard one, more work, but I've done it 40 years so I know it. Plant mid-April with film mulch. I use less fertilizer on cotton than the books say — about half a bag of compound at planting and a little urea when it starts flowering. I have to spray for bollworm and aphids 4-5 times through the summer, that's the biggest cost. My old wife and I pick by hand — at 78 my back hurts, but hired pickers are too expensive for only 2 mu. Maybe 220 kg of lint per mu if it's a good year.

**About money and labor.** My two sons work in town, send some money home, but they only come back for the busy weeks. My wife and me do most of the field work. I don't have much cash at one time, so I buy fertilizer when the agro-shop owner lets me pay after harvest. I don't take big risks — at my age, one bad year and I can't recover.
